questions.question: A team wants Copilot Chat, Copilot coding agent, and Copilot code review to follow the same coding conventions in every request made in a repository. The solution must require no action from individual developers. What should the team create?

options.text: A .github/copilot-instructions.md file in the repository
options.why: Correct. Repository custom instructions are added automatically to Copilot Chat, coding agent, and code review requests in that repository.

options.text: A .github/prompts/conventions.prompt.md file
options.why: A prompt file runs only when a developer calls it with a slash command, so it requires action from each developer.

options.text: A .vscode/settings.json file that sets github.copilot.enable
options.why: This setting turns completions on or off per language. It does not provide coding conventions.

options.text: A README.md section titled Conventions
options.why: Copilot does not automatically add a README section to every request as custom instructions.

questions.explanation: Repository-wide custom instructions belong in .github/copilot-instructions.md. Copilot Chat, the coding agent, and code review read the file automatically.

questions.question: A repository contains rules that apply only to test files in the tests folder. Developers report that Copilot applies these rules when it edits application code. You need the rules to apply only to test files. What should you do?

options.text: Move the rules to a .github/instructions/tests.instructions.md file that sets applyTo to "tests/**/*.js"
options.why: Correct. Path-specific instruction files use the applyTo glob to limit rules to matching files.

options.text: Add the text "only for tests" at the top of .github/copilot-instructions.md
options.why: Repository instructions are added to every request in the repository, so the rules would still be sent for application code.

options.text: Create a content exclusion for the tests folder
options.why: A content exclusion stops Copilot from using the files as context. It does not scope instructions.

options.text: Save the rules in .github/prompts/tests.prompt.md
options.why: A prompt file is a reusable prompt that runs on demand. It does not scope standing rules by path.

questions.explanation: Files named *.instructions.md in .github/instructions use applyTo front matter to apply rules only to matching paths.

questions.scenario: A developer saves the following file as .github/prompts/new-endpoint.prompt.md in a repository that is open in Visual Studio Code: front matter that sets mode to agent and description to "Add a REST endpoint", followed by the text "Create a new endpoint for ${input:resource} and add tests."
questions.question: How does a developer run this prompt for an orders resource in Copilot Chat?

options.text: Type /new-endpoint resource=orders in the Chat view
options.why: Correct. Prompt files in .github/prompts run as slash commands named after the file, and the input variable is filled from the text after the command.

options.text: Type @new-endpoint orders in the Chat view
options.why: The @ prefix selects a chat participant, not a prompt file.

options.text: Type #new-endpoint orders in the Chat view
options.why: The # prefix adds context such as a file. It does not run a prompt file.

options.text: Run copilot --prompt-file new-endpoint in the integrated terminal
options.why: This is not a supported way to run a VS Code prompt file.

questions.explanation: A prompt file named new-endpoint.prompt.md runs with /new-endpoint, and ${input:resource} receives the value you supply.

questions.question: Which TWO settings can you define in the front matter of a Copilot prompt file?

options.text: The chat mode or agent that runs the prompt
options.why: Correct. Prompt file front matter can set the mode, such as agent, or a custom agent.

options.text: The tools that the prompt is allowed to use
options.why: Correct. Prompt file front matter can list the tools available to the prompt.

options.text: The Copilot seats that may run the prompt
options.why: Seat assignment is managed in organization settings, not in a prompt file.

options.text: The content exclusion paths for the repository
options.why: Content exclusions are configured in repository, organization, or enterprise settings.

options.text: Whether suggestions matching public code are blocked
options.why: The public code filter is a policy setting, not prompt file front matter.

questions.explanation: Prompt file front matter can set the mode or agent, a description, the tools, and the model. Seats, exclusions, and the public code filter are administrative settings.

questions.question: A team lead wants every developer to send the same well-structured request when they ask Copilot Chat to scaffold a new service, so that the responses are consistent. The request should run only when a developer asks for it. What should the team lead create?

options.text: A prompt file in .github/prompts
options.why: Correct. A prompt file is a reusable prompt that runs on demand with a slash command, which gives consistent requests across the team.

options.text: Repository custom instructions in .github/copilot-instructions.md
options.why: Repository instructions are added to every request automatically, not only when a developer asks to scaffold a service.

options.text: A Copilot Space shared with the team
options.why: A space provides curated context for questions. It does not define a reusable request that runs on demand.

options.text: An organization policy that enables Copilot Chat in the IDE
options.why: The policy controls whether the feature is available. It does not define the request.

questions.explanation: Prompt files make a request reusable and consistent, and they run only when called. Custom instructions always apply.
